subject: Agriculture
title: Food Sovereignty
description: A fast breakdown of Food Sovereignty for builders.

hook.text: Food sovereignty says communities—not corporations or trade rules—should control their own food systems.

buildup.text: La Via Campesina—a global peasant movement of 200 million members—coined the term in 1996.

discovery.text: Food sovereignty includes the right to grow traditional crops, save seeds, and sell locally without corporate interference.

twist.text: Trade agreements often override local food policies. WTO rules can force countries to accept food imports they don't want.

climax.text: Food sovereignty is law in Ecuador, Bolivia, Mali, and Nepal. It challenges the global free-trade food model.

punchline.text: Who decides what a nation eats? The farmer or the market? That's the question.

quiz.question: What does food sovereignty demand?
options: Community control over food systems instead of corporate or trade-rule dominance

details.summary: Food sovereignty asserts the right of peoples to define their own food and agriculture systems rather than being subject to international market forces. This topic covers the movement's origins, principles, and how it challenges the dominant industrial food model.
details.whyItMatters: Food sovereignty movements argue that local communities—not corporations or trade agreements—should control their food systems. This perspective gains urgency as supply chain fragility and corporate concentration grow.
takeaways: La Vía Campesina coined the term food sovereignty at the 1996 World Food Summit
Food sovereignty prioritizes local food production for local consumption
The movement opposes corporate monopolies on seeds, land, and water resources

faq.question: What is food sovereignty?
faq.answer: Food sovereignty is the right of peoples to healthy and culturally appropriate food produced through ecologically sound methods, and their right to define their own food and agriculture systems. It prioritizes local needs over export-driven production.

faq.question: How does food sovereignty differ from food security?
faq.answer: Food security focuses on ensuring people have enough to eat regardless of source. Food sovereignty goes further by demanding communities control how food is produced, traded, and distributed, emphasizing local production, farmer rights, and ecological sustainability.
